channel.title: The Journal Record - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Journal Record (journalrecord.com)

item.title: Oklahoma lawmakers send voter ID state question to August ballot
item.description: Oklahoma lawmakers approved Senate Joint Resolution 47 to place a voter ID constitutional amendment on the August 25 primary runoff ballot.

item.title: On the Town: Legacy luncheon, Yukon farm tour, ACM honors
item.description: The Junior League of Oklahoma City honored members at its legacy luncheon, Yukon’s Mollie Spencer Farm hosts spring open house, and Oklahoma venues receive ACM nominations.

item.title: Paycom, BOK named ACM Arena of the Year finalists
item.description: Paycom Center and BOK Center named ACM Arena of the Year finalists as Oklahoma venues gain national attention.

item.title: Property tax exemption measure faces Oklahoma Supreme Court challenge
item.description: The Oklahoma Supreme Court is set to consider a protest that could block State Question 843, which proposes exempting owner-occupied homes from property taxes.

item.title: Free Market Friday: School-choice opponents think everyone is ‘rich’
item.description: Opinion: Oklahoma school choice tax credit debate centers on income, with data showing most families are low- to middle-income.

item.title: OKC Comets to open 2026 season at Chickasaw Bricktown Ballpark
item.description: The Oklahoma City Comets will open their 2026 season at Chickasaw Bricktown Ballpark with a three-game series against the Albuquerque Isotopes.

item.title: Capital Perspectives: Thoughts &amp; observations over the Iranian conflict
item.description: Chas Craig analyzes the Iran conflict's impact on energy prices, inflation, and investment strategies amid global economic uncertainty.

item.title: Dollar rises as optimism fades for swift end to Middle East war
item.description: The dollar edged higher amid doubts about a quick resolution to the Middle East conflict, with inflation concerns and energy price rises impacting markets.

item.title: All-female First American law firm opens in Tahlequah
item.description: Tribal Justice Advocacy &amp; Law, an all-female First American law firm, opens in Tahlequah to serve tribal clients with experienced former prosecutors.

item.title: Calm Waters reimagines annual fundraiser as circus dinner show
item.description: Calm Waters Center for Children and Families transforms its annual fundraiser in Oklahoma City into a theatrical circus dinner show to support grief services.

item.title: Oklahoma Quality Foundation to host 2026 Excellence Summit in Oklahoma City
item.description: The Oklahoma Quality Foundation will hold its 2026 Oklahoma Excellence Summit in Oklahoma City, featuring leaders from multiple sectors and awards presentations.

item.title: First American sorority makes history at East Central University
item.description: Gamma Delta Pi, a national sorority for First American women, launched its first chapter at East Central University in Ada, marking a historic milestone.

item.title: Traders bet $500M on oil price just before Trump’s post on delay to Iran attack
item.description: Traders wagered over $500 million on crude oil futures just minutes before President Donald Trump announced a delay to attacks on Iran, causing oil prices to plunge.

item.title: Women’s Resource Center names interim director as longtime leader retires
item.description: Women's Resource Center in Norman appoints Ajia Meux-Jacobs as interim director following Kristy Stewart's retirement after 42 years of service.

item.title: Oklahoma governor selects Alan Armstrong to replace Markwayne Mullin
item.description: Gov. Kevin Stitt appointed Alan Armstrong, former Williams Companies CEO, to replace Markwayne Mullin in the U.S. Senate.
